title: Compact Token Thrift Widget: inline batching/cache suggestions with safe-apply flow
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: design a compact, embeddable 'Token Thrift' widget that surfaces recommended batching and cache presets inline within route and model configuration screens. The widget should provide a concise recommendation, an explainable risk score, and a one-click safe-apply flow that creates a canary rollout. This ticket contains the prototype spec, rationale, trade-offs, and user test plan.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype (Figma) demonstrates widget in two contexts: Route Settings and Model Version settings
Widget shows top-2 suggested presets, explanation snippets, estimated token savings and latency impact
Safe-apply flow creates a canary rollout entry in Console UI and surfaces rollback action
Design review signoff from PM and Eng and 5 moderated usability sessions with SRE/Platform engineers
Documentation copy (short explainer + tooltip text) committed to docs repo and linked from widget
design_notes: Compact layout is 320px wide to permit insertion into right rail and modal footers
Primary CTA: 'Apply as canary' triggers pipeline that creates a canary route with 10% traffic and attaches batching/cache presets
Secondary CTA: 'Preview impact' opens a lightweight simulator showing 1-hour token cost and 95th percentile latency delta
Risk score combines model compatibility (architecture tags), prefix-cache hit probability, and production SLO impact; displayed as Low/Med/High with hover explainer
Default suggestion derives from workload signature (conversation vs. stateless completion) and historical per-route seq length distribution from observability
Guardrail: if suggestion reduces latency but increases hallucination risk (based on prior quality regressions for similar presets), show an explicit warning and require review
Copy should avoid jargon; use 'token savings' rather than 'throughput efficiency' in primary view
Design should allow pausing auto-suggest for projects with strict experimental policies (opt-out toggle)
tradeoffs_and_alternatives: Inline compact widget vs. full-screen composer: compact preserves context but limits advanced controls; we propose link to full composer for expert users
Automated canary apply vs. manual export: auto-apply reduces friction but increases blast radius; mitigate by requiring codeowner or SRE approval for high-risk changes
Expose numeric heuristics vs. human-readable tags: numbers (expected tokens saved) are persuasive but can be misleading for non-technical PMs; include both
Aggressive caching presets may conflict with privacy/compliance constraints in Private deployments; suggestions must run compliance check before apply
engineering_notes: Requires new lightweight recommendation API endpoint: /v1/console/suggest-presets (bounded 200ms target)
Backfill: observability team to provide per-route distribution metrics (median/95th seq lengths, cache hit estimates)
Canary creation integrates with existing rollout service; default 10% traffic for 1 hour with automated rollback on error rate increase >2x
Frontend: build widget as a reusable React component that can mount in right rail, modal footer, and route list expanded row
Telemetry: track suggestion impressions, apply rate, preview views, and rollback events for ROI analysis
usability_plan: Recruit 5 engineers (SRE/Platform) + 3 product PMs for moderated sessions
Tasks: 1) Interpret suggestion and explain why recommended 2) Run preview and read simulator output 3) Apply canary and find rollback action
Success metrics: 80% can complete safe-apply without prompting, 90% understand risk warning text
Collect SUS and open-text feedback, tag recurrent confusion points for copy/visual tweaks
open_questions: What threshold defines 'high' risk for guardrail blocking (probabilistic vs. deterministic)?
Should canary percentage default be configurable per-org (enterprise customers) or fixed for simplicity?
Who signs off on proposals that change quantization/disabling of prefix caching in Private deployments?
Do we include an opt-in A/B experiment for auto-apply suggestions to measure impact on token spend?
